Question: Which of the following options will not enhance the yield of a reaction at equilibrium?

Options:
A. Increasing the scale of the reaction
B. Removal of a product by crystallization
C. Removal of a product by distillation
D. Using a reactant in excess

Thought: I need to analyze each option to determine which one will not enhance the yield of a reaction at equilibrium. Let me consider each option carefully.

According to Le Chatelier's principle, when a chemical system at equilibrium is disturbed, the equilibrium shifts to counteract the disturbance and establish a new equilibrium.

A. Increasing the scale of the reaction - This simply means making more of the reaction mixture, but with the same proportions of reactants. Scaling up a reaction doesn't change the equilibrium position or the yield percentage. It just produces more total product while maintaining the same yield percentage.

B. Removal of a product by crystallization - If a product is removed from the equilibrium mixture (by crystallizing it out), the equilibrium will shift to produce more of that product, increasing the yield.

C. Removal of a product by distillation - Similar to crystallization, removing a product by distillation will shift the equilibrium toward producing more product, increasing the yield.

D. Using a reactant in excess - According to Le Chatelier's principle, increasing the concentration of a reactant will shift the equilibrium toward the products, increasing the yield.

Based on this analysis, increasing the scale of the reaction (option A) will not enhance the yield percentage of a reaction at equilibrium. It will produce more total product, but the percentage yield remains the same.
Final Answer: [ANSWER]A[/ANSWER]
